title: What is known about 1RB0RE_1RC0RA_0LD0LB_0LA1LE_1LC1LF_0LA---
description: Proof status of the six-state BB(6) holdout 1RB0RE_1RC0RA_0LD0LB_0LA1LE_1LC1LF_0LA---.
intro: Nobody knows whether this six-state, two-symbol Turing machine halts when started on a blank tape: it is one of the holdouts left open by the bbchallenge project. This page lists what has been established about it, sorted by what each result rests on.
verdict: The question is open. The run is an exact pass map: sampled at the left end, the tape is a counter and a list of blocks (10)^m, and each pass changes it only at the counter and at one frontier, by about a dozen rules with exact step counts. The map is checked pass by pass to 1.1·109 steps, and an accelerated simulator built on it goes to 7.9·1010 steps. Lean proves the main rule (a block grows by 4 while the next one shrinks) for every list of blocks. The other rules are not yet proved, and the long-term behaviour of the list is not known.

claims.title: The halting configurations
claims.text: The machine stops exactly when it reads the symbol of a halting transition (F1); the generated statement covers every configuration.

claims.title: No halt in the first 10,000 steps
claims.text: The list simulator of the shared library, proved to agree with the machine's semantics, runs 10,000 steps from blank tape without a halt, evaluated by Lean's kernel.

claims.title: No halt in the first 10<sup>7</sup> steps
claims.text: The same run, evaluated by compiled code.

claims.title: No halt in the first 10<sup>9</sup> steps
claims.text: The C simulator tools/c/triage.c runs 109 steps without a halt; at the end 63,402 cells have been visited and 33,328 of them hold a 1.

claims.title: Shift rules of a pass
claims.text: left_end, left_block, right_end and the six rules pass_start, pass_right, pass_front, pass_sep, pass_left, pass_end: the pieces of one pass from the left end to the frontier and back, each for every block length and every surrounding tape.

claims.title: The block-growing pass, for every list
claims.text: With S = 1 1 1 0 1, blk n = (10)^(n+3) S and front p q = (10)^(p+3) 1 (10)^(q+3) 1 1 1 0: for every c, p, q, every list of blocks m1..mk and every tape R, 0^inf A> 1 0 0 blk(c+1) blk(m1)...blk(mk) front(p, q+1) R reaches 0^inf A> 1 0 0 blk(c) blk(m1)...blk(mk) front(p+4, q) R. This is rule c of the pass map. The proof is by induction over the list.

claims.title: The pass map
claims.text: Sampled at each arrival at the left end in state A, the tape is a 0 a^c and a list of pairs 1^k a^n (a = 10). One pass changes only the counter c and the first place where the list stops alternating separators (2,1) and blocks (1,m). The rules (counter phase, block grows, next block, carry, timer, rebuild, and a few rare ones) come with step formulas such as 6c+20F+6M+6p+56. Replaying every one of the 16,064 passes from step 440 to step 1,099,824,330 gives the plain machine's tape and step count exactly. The rare rules h, i and f2 are checked on the tape only.

claims.title: No halt in the first 7.9·10<sup>10</sup> steps
claims.text: The accelerated simulator py/accsim.py applies runs of identical passes at once, with exact step counts. It agrees with the plain machine (state and step) at all 72 batch ends up to step 2,782,338,426 and in windows of plain simulation at steps 4.89·1010 and 5.29·1010. It runs to step 79,277,382,450 (164,003 passes, 13 rebuilds) without a halt, and stops there at a case its rules do not cover.

claims.title: Rebuilds
claims.text: When the counter runs out, the first block becomes the next counter. The counter blocks of the 13 rebuilds are 6, 10, 18, 66, 130, 258, 1026, 4098, 16386, 258, 3078, 3364 and 16590. A block grows by 4 per pass while the frontier eats its neighbour, so sizes 4<sup>k</sup>+2 appear. A frontier that is still open at a rebuild stays in the list as a bare block or a frozen carry.

claims.title: Why it is hard
claims.text: Each rule is local and simple, but the counter at each round is set by the first block, and the frontier freezes wherever the counter runs out. That leaves new kinds of items in the list (a bare block, a frozen carry). A proof needs a finite set of item kinds that the map preserves, and the run keeps finding new combinations (the latest at step 79,277,382,450).

explainer.lede: Nobody knows. The machine sweeps over a list of blocks. Each pass changes only a counter and one place in the list, the frontier, by a small set of exact rules. When the counter runs out, the first block becomes the next counter.

facts.text: No halt, by an accelerated simulator built on the exact pass map.
Lean proves the main pass rule for any list of blocks.
Each matches the plain machine exactly, to 1.1·10<sup>9</sup> steps.

sections.heading: A counter, a list and a frontier
html: Look at the tape each time the head comes back to the left end in state A, and write a for 10. The tape reads a 0 a^c followed by a list of pairs 1^k a^n. Normally the list alternates separators 1 1 a and blocks 1 a^m. The first place where it does not is the frontier.
One pass, from the left end to the frontier and back, changes only the counter c and the frontier. The main rules:

rulebeforeaftersteps
counter phasec, (1,q) firstc+3, (1,q−1)6c+36
block grows(1,p)(1,q)(1,p+4)(1,q−1)6c+20F+6M+6p+56
next block(1,p)(3,1)(1,m)(1,p)(2,1)(1,4)(1,m−1)6c+20F+6M+6p+74
carry(2,q)(2,1)(1,m)(2,1)(1,q+3)(2,m)6c+20F+6M+8q+48
timerno frontiera block (1,1) added at the end6c+20F+6M+44

F and M are the number of blocks left of the frontier and the sum of their lengths, and c drops by one in every pass except in the counter phase. A block grows by 4 per pass while it eats the next one, so a block m comes out as 4m. When c runs out, a rebuild turns the first block into the next counter. That is why the counters jump: 66, 258, 1026, 4098, 16386, ... (4k+2).

sections.heading: What is proved and what is missing
html: Every pass up to 1.1·109 steps was replayed with these rules and matched the machine exactly, step count included. An accelerated simulator that applies whole runs of passes at once reaches 7.9·1010 steps with no halt.

Lean proves the block grows rule for every counter, every frontier and every list of blocks in between (pass in lean/Pass.lean), by induction over the list from the pieces of one pass. The other rules still need the same treatment. Beyond that, a proof of non-halting needs a description of all the lists the map can reach. When the counter runs out in the middle of the list, the frontier freezes and leaves a new kind of item behind, and the run keeps producing new combinations of these.

sections.heading: The shape of the run
html: Left of the start, the visited part of the tape grows like the square root of the step count, the signature of a head sweeping back and forth across the whole tape and adding a cell or a few at the end of each sweep (a bouncer-like shape) (fitted exponent 0.455). Right of the start it stopped growing in the second half of the run (bounded so far, or growing so slowly that no record fell in the last half).
After 109 steps the tape spans 63,402 cells (49,572 left of the start, 1,101 right), with a density of 1s of 0.526.
These are measurements of one bounded run, sorted by tools/py/bbtools/triage.py; the macro structure behind them is the next thing to find.

sections.heading: Related machines
html: Other holdouts of the list of 608 that are tied to this one. The comparison of tables is exact; everything about runs was checked on the first 107 steps of each machine and is an observation, not a proof (holdouts/related.py, holdouts/related.json).

Same table as the machine below, started in another state. Renaming the states as shown turns this machine's table into the other one, the halting transition included. The other machine starts in its own state A, which is not this machine's A: its run from blank tape is the run of this table started in another state. These are different runs: in the first 107 steps of each, no configuration of this machine's run occurs in the other, even up to a shift of the tape. So each of these holdouts is its own halting question, and settling one does not settle another.

summary: An exact pass map on a counter and a list of blocks (10)^m: each pass changes only the counter and one frontier, where a block grows by 4 while it eats its neighbour; checked pass by pass to 1.1e9 steps, accelerated to 7.9e10; Lean proves the block-growing pass for every list.
